reviews.title: WARNING: HIDDEN WEB SUBSCRIPTION SCAM!
reviews.text:
Do not trust this app! They run a massive billing trap. If you take their quiz or click an ad online, they sign you up for a hidden web subscription that does NOT show up in your Apple ID.
Even if you download the app and cancel your trial through Apple (and get the cancellation email), they will STILL secretly charge your credit card for a full-priced web subscription. They run two separate billing systems to trick you into thinking you are canceled while they keep stealing your money. Customer service is unhelpful and refuses refunds. Avoid at all costs, or check your bank statements carefully!

reviews.title: Not accurate
reviews.text: In fairness, I’m a PhD immunologist with over 20 years of experience in the field. There are a few questions I have encountered so far that are problematic. For example one question asked if the lungs are part of the immune system. The answer here said no. But the answer is yes. The cilia and mucus that line the airways help to bind and remove infectious agents. There are specialized immune cells that reside in the lungs that will stimulate an immune response if a pathogen is detected. Same goes for the nose. The reality is that body parts often have more than one function. Your skin is considered to be an immune organ because it acts as a barrier and because it is loaded with potent immune cells. Another issue I had was a question on whether pink eye is infectious. The answer is it depends. Pink eye can be caused by allergens, which is not infectious. If it’s viral or bacterial then it is infectious. While this is all acceptable for something meant for fun, when you charge the money you are charging for this app, I expect a bit more.

reviews.title: DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP. NIBBLE IS A PREDATORY, SOUL-CRUSHING SCAM!
reviews.text:
DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP. NIBBLE IS A PREDATORY, SOUL-CRUSHING SCAM DISGUISED AS “EDUCATION.” I signed up for what they slyly call a “free trial,” and within minutes—before I could even blink—they slammed my card with a full charge like a mugger in a dark alley. Surprise! Your “free” trial is a bait-and-switch trap designed to steal your money instantly. No warning, no grace period, just straight-up theft. If I could rate their billing practices zero stars, I’d give them minus a million. Contacted support? Good luck navigating their useless black hole of canned responses while they clutch your cash like Gollum with his precious.
And the content? Oh sweet baby Jesus, it’s an insult to human intelligence. These “bite-sized lessons” feel like they were scripted by a committee of bored kindergarten teachers on heavy sedatives—for actual eight-year-olds. Cartoonish animations, baby-talk explanations of basic concepts, and quizzes that wouldn’t challenge a goldfish with brain damage. I came expecting to spark curiosity as an adult, not regress to finger-painting level drivel about topics dumbed down so far they circle back to insulting. “Interactive 10-minute lessons”? More like 10 minutes of eye-rolling torture wondering how this garbage ever got approved for anyone over the age of 10.0
This app isn’t “expanding your understanding”—it’s a cash-grab parasite sucking money from people desperate for self-improvement while delivering content so infantile it makes me question the entir

reviews.title: Asked to rate before setup completed
reviews.text: There’s a lengthy set of questions before you can do anything. Halfway through you are asked to rate the app which seems a little premature. Once you’re finished you’re then told you have to sign up to a £90 subscription at the end of a week’s free trial before you can try the app. It’s a shame this isn’t made clear at the beginning.  If you forget to cancel then they’ve made some easy money. It might be better to offer a limited version of the app so that people can truly try it for free.

reviews.title: Good app but yet another subscription based app
reviews.text: I liked the range of things you can learn and learn at your own pace but frankly I’m sick of all these subscription based apps. You HAVE to set up a subscription in order to use the app. It should be free but optional to pay for more content. Ridiculous how subscriptions are a simple click but to cancel them it’s deliberately designed to have so many more steps to make it difficult to opt out. Save your money and don’t bother downloading

reviews.title: Scammy business practices
reviews.text: Buyer beware: if you no longer want this app, make sure you do more than cancel your subscription. Be EXPLICIT in your email to cancel every single portion of your subscription, as there are parts that won’t automatically be cancelled. For example, I cancelled my subscription and kept getting billed at a lesser rate the following month because I didn’t specify that I wanted all parts (infographics included) cancelled. Then, they supposedly cancelled it but I got billed yet again the following month. I logged into the app which I had not yet deleted and went into my profile to delete my method of payment and it isn’t there.  According to the app, I no longer seem to have an account even though my email and password still work, yet I am still being charged. I continue to email them and decided to share this horrible experience so this doesn’t happen to other people. Very scammy.

reviews.title: AI Slop-Filled, Non-Refundable, and Soullessly Greedy
reviews.text:
Hi everyone,
Just wanted to share that this app is terrible and soulless — they desperately beg you to buy their subscription (even if you unsubscribe from their messaging), lower it to a somewhat reasonable price, and then automatically charge you three times that when tapping through their ridiculous onboarding. The “features” I received (that I didn’t want in the first place) from the $30 extra were a sloppy AI-generated textbook and a similarly-generated repetitive “productivity” document that I could’ve created myself for cheaper. Additionally, the app itself seems appealing, but gives useless information that could be easily searched with less costly AI tools. I personally can’t believe this costs money to use, and the fact that it charged me extra is even worse. Cool-sounding concept, terrible in execution.

- A Human Being

reviews.title: SCAM AND PREDATORY
reviews.text:
If I could, it would be 0 stars. I didn’t have it downloaded for more than 2 minutes and I hated it. I answered the whole questionnaire and wanted to check out the app. I kid you not, every 2 seconds there was a pop up telling me to sign up and pay a subscription. Nothing worked, and someone said even with the free trial, none of the things they offered worked. 0/10.. horrible pop-ups. Also definitely fake reviews for anything above 2 stars. ALSO, THERE IS NO FREE TRIAL!!!! it says this… “If you start a free trial, you will be automatically charged a price indicated on the payment screen for a chosen subscription period unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the free trial.
Note that deleting the app does not cancel your subscriptions.!!” so they still charge you even if you click free trial. what a scam.

reviews.title: Okay content, poor customer service
reviews.text:
I got this app thinking it would be a great way to learn some new pieces of trivia in my down time. For a short while it did exactly that. It’s an overall well made app that has good lessons on some interesting topics, and it’s easy to follow. For a few days I enjoyed it.

For me, the lessons were too entry level and I quickly grew bored of them so I cancelled. No big deal right?  I thought it would an easy cancel and that’s it. Unfortunately that has not been the case… I have tried to cancel three times now and each time I have gotten confirmation that this subscription is over, and then I get charged the next month!

I will probably not get my money back for an app I haven’t used since the start, so please think before you get the subscription! The customer service is a joke, and won’t let you cancel once you buy. So now I have to cancel this through my bank. I hope this will save someone else the terrible experience I’ve had

Didn’t show up in my active subscriptions so I didn’t have any options to cancel it and then I’ve been charged £60 without any warning or communication! Fraudsters, don’t waste your time or money.

reviews.title: read please
reviews.text: If i could give this app 0 stars, I would. First, you can’t really do anything until you pay. I had gotten the app thinking i could use it. WRONG. I stoped using the app for a while and recently decided to get on it. i was then presented with a 7 day free trial. I was ecstatic because i wanted to use the app but I didn’t care to pay for a subscription. I proceeded to do the process and then a few moments afterwards, I see a notification in my phone that my card was trying to get charged for the annual subscription for this app. unbelievable. mind you, as soon as i did everything to get the free trial, i immediately cancelled it and had noticed that it said a date for next year. and then that happens and i’m baffled. this app is a total scam

reviews.title: Surprise upcharges
reviews.text: I subscribed to the app for 3 months and after I purchased, there was options for additional up charges. I clicked on one to see what it entailed and it immediately purchased that as well. I asked for a refund the same day but all purchases are non-refundable. How convenient.  *Update: since you wanna lie… I emailed support the same day explaining the additional upcharge was a mistake and it was never my intention to purchase it and I didn’t even know what it was. Support said the same thing you’re saying with this response, there are no mistakes etc. Just fix your checkout process to be more transparent, that’s literally all you have to do. If a customer clicks on something, allow them to confirm purchase and even better, let them research what they clicked on before confirming. To make your checkout process like this and then say no refunds even if it’s the same day, is predatory.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your time or money
reviews.text: I messaged to cancel my infographics subscription and asked for a refund as the purchase was accidental (the infographics subscription is an additional feature to the base subscription). I was not prompted to approve a separate charge to my account outside of the base subscription. The charge to my account was instead automatically approved upon selection, which I initially thought was just leading me to another page for further information about the additional feature. They won’t give me refund even though the user interface is misleading at best. According to their terms & condition “Terms and Conditions (clause 5.8), purchases made via our website are non-refundable and non-exchangeable” but they also don’t guarantee refunds for purchases made on the app, so I guess that means they hate their customers.

The cartoonish graphics reinforce the the idea that it's aimed at kids. I don't know if I have the patience to see if persistence leads to something more challenging.

The app is sized for phone so makes poor use of the iPad screen. And now it is stuck on the “Nailed It” screen after I answered just 3 questions. Unusable. 

I wish I hadn't wasted my money on this.

reviews.title: Great concept let down by use of generative ai
reviews.text: A wonderful idea to tackle doomscrolling however it’s a shame it’s full of generative ai images and bots. Not only is generative ai harmful to the environment but also well known to provide inaccurate or false information. How can you trust a learning app that heavily relies on something that’s been proven to provide incorrect content, especially when paying £18 a month or £90 a year for that info.

reviews.title: Fraudulent and misleading app
reviews.text:
Their social media advert was completely misguided and fraudulent. I expected this app to have topics and the difficulty I was expecting from what the advert portrayed.

One purchasing nibble and navigating the app, I realised that what I was expecting was not offered at all and was fraudulently advertised. 

I was promised a 30 day money back guarantee. Beware, this is a lie, I was not given my money back “as per the terms and conditions”. Although it clearly stated 30 day money back guarantee, I was not given anything in compensation. Additionally, I only navigated through the app and emailed to cancel as I was disappointed within an hour of purchasing. I clearly had not taken the app for granted and wished my money back. 

This app has lied to me about its contents and essentially stolen my money.

This app is for useless trivia nonsense and does not offer structured/comprehensive learning in any topic.

Be aware and DO NOT purchase this app. I hope this helps others before falling into this trap

I have reported to Apple as fraudulent app. 

I DO NOT want your generic reply saying to email you as I have tried that and you have not been helpful. So if that is all you’re going to offer then don’t bother.


H

reviews.title: Falsely Advertised
reviews.text:
If there’s one thing I don’t care for, it’s fake advertising because I’m not going to play the fool and be lied to my face and then suckered into paying for a subscription before actually using the app. 
I was on social media when the advertisement for Nibble came up and it was described as an Entymology learning app. Sign me up! I’m definitely that weirdo that loves bugs. After going through such a lengthy onboarding process and picking what I wanted to learn about, Entymology was not an option. I skipped the subscription screen because I want to know what I’m buying and test the app out. When I say I was disappointed, I scrolled through what was provided to me and found it boring and a waste of time. Nothing that was really fascinating. It all seemed unfortunately limited

reviews.title: Just awful
reviews.text:
I don’t understand why certain apps force you into these payment plans. 

You spend 5 minutes going through this whole tailored profiling to sort out recommendation then get payment plans shovelled down your throat, print asking for reviews, payments trial this but cancel here.

It’s hardly an app worth spending 5 minutes to set up if you’re not even allowed to listen to one story without subscribing to anything? How am I suppose to know if I enjoy the co tent without even being able to enjoy the content without subscribing to something. Yes you can opt in for a free trial then pay at the end but you’re still forced to sign up to something to access ANY content. It’s just boring, at least let me trial 1 book or 1 listen.

There’s so many better apps than this tbh at allow the same principles without the force feeding of reviews this pay for that. 

Don’t even waste your time

reviews.title: A scam
reviews.text: After being lured by the free trial, I used it for a couple days and then got boring, then I totally forgot about it and they charged me £120 a year, then I said oh ok what the H. It was my fault for forgetting and now that I cancelled it said I could still access to the content for the whole year, and I have proof that No I can’t. I have not been able to access to the content on my app. And of course I know no refunds will be made on this. Totally my fault for trusting an “educative app” who doesn’t not even take care on reminding you a payment is coming soon. Completely dishonest. Do not recommend and the little content it has is not worthy.

reviews.title: Worth reading
reviews.text: Nearly 30 questions with yawn-worthy AI in a format that’s overplayed. Then to proceed with a trial, no initial price posted until you click “proceed with free trial” so it’s false commitment, a psychology test that won’t work because people will see the price and think “that was a waste, not doing this”. Yes you’ll get some people who don’t care and will by any app but ultimately you’re actual active user numbers will peak and dip into a valley known as the Law of Diminishing Return.  Not only did it waste my time on that pre sign up UX/UI, but now you’re going to have to face the reality that a high bounce rate is everything in marketing and go-to-market strategy. Make this app free for students, make it freemium for the mass population, and make an ad free one that’s $9.99 a month or $99 one time payment. Allocate revenue from ads to sponsor scholarships for students who achieve learning streaks on the app. Create brand awareness on college campuses, trade schools, anywhere people are learning, there’s Nibble. Nibble: What did YOU learn today?
